title: Psychological Resilience Among Young Children in West Nusa Tenggara After Natural Disasters: A Systematic Literature Review
content: Purpose – This review synthesizes empirical evidence on psychological resilience among young children (0–8 years) after natural disasters, identifying protective factors and their implications for early childhood education (ECE) in West Nusa Tenggara (NTB), Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach – Following PRISMA 2020, studies published between January 2015 and June 2026 were searched in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, ERIC, and Google Scholar. Eligible studies [DATA DIPERLUKAN: jumlah studi yang diinklusi] were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT, 2018) and synthesized thematically around four research questions. Findings – Disaster exposure is associated with neurobiological, cognitive, and emotional disruption in children from birth to eight years, with effects traceable even to prenatal stress. Recovery, however, depends less on individual traits than on the systems surrounding the child: caregiver stability, restored routines, trauma-informed ECE settings, and culturally embedded solidarity. In NTB, Gotong Royong (Sasak), Saling Satingi (Samawa), Makariki (Mbojo), and religious coping appear to function as informal psychosocial infrastructure. Play-based and trauma-informed pedagogical approaches show promise, although rigorous evidence from post-disaster ECE settings in Indonesia remains scarce. Originality/value – The review addresses the age-group asymmetry in disaster resilience research and proposes an Integrated Systemic Educational Model that positions the ECE center as a hub linking global resilience frameworks with local ethno-parenting practices in disaster-prone archipelagic regions.
